headline: South Asia: Riyadh airport suspends operations after attack leaves several wounded
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Riyadh airport suspends operations after attack leaves several wounded.
- Asia: Russian attacks kill 20 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin.
- Persian Gulf Region: Iran retains missile, drone production capabilities despite months of US-Israeli strikes - report.

Full breakdown follows.

United States - bottom line: Pentagon, Raytheon sign $6.3B deal to replenish US missile interceptor supply.
- Military Times, one day ago: Pentagon, Raytheon sign $6.3B deal to replenish US missile interceptor supply.
The contract "supports urgent replenishment of missile defense inventory that has been successfully used in combat," Raytheon said.
The Caribbean - bottom line: StJMC mulls action against companies for hanging wires.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 15 hours ago: StJMC mulls action against companies for hanging wires.
WESTERN BUREAU: The St James Municipal Corporation is calling on telecommunications companies with low-hanging wires, which were displaced by Hurricane Melissa a year ago, to address them immediately or risk legal action in the interest of the public safety. Montego Bay Mayor Richard Vernon issued the warning on Thursday at the St James Municipal Corporation’s (StJMC) City Hall 2026 Municipal Budget Presentation at the Montego Bay Cultural Centre, where he outlined plans for the corporation’s $2.8-billion budget expenditure for the 2027-2028 financial year.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

The death toll following the Russian airstrike on Zaporizhzhia has risen to 20, including three children, and 18 others have been injured.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Ukraine strikes Samara oil facility again, Russian command posts and electronic warfare station also hit.
Ukraine's defence forces struck the Samara linear production dispatching station in Russia's Samara Oblast, along with Russian command posts and an electronic warfare station on the night of 9-10 October.

An 11-year-old boy has been killed and two other children have been injured in a Russian drone attack on the Nikopol district in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast.

Trump's remarks leave open the possibility of direct US military involvement alongside Saudi Arabia against the Houthis. He also added that he thought 'it's time for Ukraine to get a new president.'

A rare pair of waterspouts swept ashore in western Sicily on Friday, damaging homes, vehicles and a school. The two funnels formed off the coast near Marsala before moving inland towards Trapani, hitting the town of Petrosino along the way.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Riyadh airport suspends operations after attack leaves several wounded.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, ABC News Australia, Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Riyadh airport suspends operations after attack leaves several wounded.
Saudi authorities suspended operations at Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday after a fresh attack there left multiple people wounded. The Saudi civil aviation authority confirmed an attack had injured several people at the sprawling King Khalid International Airport, with a diplomatic source attributing it to a missile fired by Yemen’s Houthi rebels. The situation prompted health officials to activate a rare mass call-up of doctors to deal with the “serious emergency”, a medical source said, while foreign embassies warned their citizens to avoid the facility.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, 14 hours ago: Trump sows doubt on plan to livestream US military execution.
US President Donald Trump has cast doubt on whether authorities will livestream the firing squad execution of the perpetrator of a deadly attack on American soldiers, a plan that has drawn broad and bipartisan condemnation, it emerged on Saturday. Nidal Hasan’s execution — scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 — is set to be the first by a US military firing squad since 1945.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: 10 terrorists killed during CTD operation in Barkhan, says Balochistan govt.
QUETTA: Ten terrorists were killed in a targeted intelligence-based operation conducted by the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) in Balochistan’s Barkhan district, the Home Department said on Saturday. An aide in the Home Department, Babar Yousafzai, said: “During an intense gun battle, 10 armed terrorists were killed and two CTD officials were injured.” The CTD had conducted a targeted operation after receiving credible information about the presence of terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy, Fitna al Hindustan, in the area, according to Yousafzai.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: Pakistan reaffirms commitment to Saudi security at UN Security Council.
UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan has reaffirmed its commitment to Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security at the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), declaring that it would stand “shoulder to shoulder” with the kingdom in the face of continued Houthi attacks.

Russian strikes killed at least 20 people in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, Ukrainian officials said on Saturday, a day after US President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel that Kyiv warned would help bankroll Moscow’s war in Ukraine. Three children were among those killed when Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said on Saturday. Australia has no need to buy fuel from Russia and said that purchases from there would remain barred so that the country did not benefit from the invasion of Ukraine. “We don’t need or want Russian fuel in Australia,” Chris Bowen, Australia’s minister for climate change and energy, said on Saturday at a press conference in western Sydney. “We do not want Vladimir Putin to benefit from this war in the Middle East. What the United States does is a matter for them, but we won’t be changing our...

Police detained more than 2,000 protesters and the founder of the “cockroach” youth movement in Delhi on Saturday as security forces locked down parts of the capital to thwart a demonstration demanding the resignation of India’s election chief. - Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Utah couple cycles 3,634 miles across America, raises $23,000 for charities.
A couple from Utah marked their 40th wedding anniversary with an epic cycling adventure across the United States, covering more than 3,600 miles in 87 days. Their mission was to raise awareness and funds for affordable housing and food assistance. Along the way, they navigated diverse terrains and overcame significant obstacles, bringing attention to the plight of families grappling with housing and food insecurity.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Florida cybersecurity owner accused of secretly paying hackers over $8 million.
Zohar Pinhasi, the owner of MonsterCloud, faces charges of wire fraud related to his cybersecurity business. Prosecutors allege he misrepresented his firm's capabilities to clients facing ransomware attacks. Instead of recovering data without ransom payment, he secretly paid attackers and charged clients significantly higher fees. Pinhasi allegedly collected over $19 million while paying more than $8 million in ransoms.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Rob Parker criticises undefeated Vikings as offense struggles to score touchdowns.
The Minnesota Vikings are 4-0, but Rob Parker believes their poor offense makes them the NFL’s weakest unbeaten team. Two victories without an offensive touchdown have raised concerns, even as their defense and kicker Will Reichard keep delivering results. Minnesota now needs to improve its attack to prove its perfect start reflects genuine strength.
